title: deprecate-legacy-kafka-load-proxy-introduce-typed-scenarios
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The existing load-test ingestion path uses a legacy Kafka proxy shim that serializes scenarios into an opaque byte blob and requires runtime schema guesses. This causes flaky deserialization errors, opaque metrics (no scenario-level breakdown), and prevents deterministic scenario replay across harness versions. It's also pinned to an old Java library and blocks bumping client dependencies.

Goal: Replace the legacy Kafka load proxy with a typed-scenarios ingestion pipeline + small compatibility façade. Deliverables: (1) new typed scenario protobuf format and validator, (2) a Rust-based lightweight producer/adapter that emits typed messages to existing Kafka topics, (3) a compatibility consumer to support older test runners for a transitional period, (4) add scenario-level telemetry (scenario_id, seed, deterministic_hash) to the perf metrics pipeline, and (5) upgrade the Java client dep to 3.x by removing the pinned proxy code path.

Why this matters: Typed scenarios enable deterministic replay (reduce noise), improve our perf regression signal-to-noise ratio, and unblock dependency upgrades across the harness. Also allows future KV-cache and prefix-caching probes to be annotated per-scenario for more granular perf tuning.
acceptance_criteria: New protobuf schema defined and documented in Confluence (link below)
Rust producer (adapter) passes CI smoke and integration tests and is published as container image redwood/load-adapter:typed-2026.03
Compatibility consumer supports reading legacy opaque blobs and converting them to typed messages for at least one release cycle
Perf regression jobs show reduced variance for targeted scenarios (p95 variance drop > 35% for the three noisy workloads in benchmark-goldset)
All harness clients can opt-in to typed messages via config flag, default remains backward-compatible until full rollout
No production-facing changes to hosted API; this is test harness-only and gated behind namespaces and flags
tasks: Draft protobuf schema and run vetting session with runtime and SDK teams
Implement Rust adapter + CI build and containerize
Implement lightweight compatibility consumer (Java) that can translate legacy blob -> typed proto
Add schema validator to harness CI and local run scripts
Emit scenario_id and deterministic_hash tags to tracing and metrics
Run staged canary: run 10% of nightly jobs with typed producer and compare metrics
Coordinate Java client bump after compatibility consumer is validated
Add docs and migration guide for internal teams and SREs
comments: 2026-02-22 - Aisha Patel: Spiked schema options. Two shapes looked promising: (A) compact protobuf with optional fields for hybrid scenarios, (B) JSON-schema driven approach. Went with protobuf to keep wire size down and make deterministic hashing trivial.
2026-02-25 - Marcus Li: Pushed initial proto + README to RFC. Waiting on runtime team for KV cache annotation shape. I scheduled a sync with @Elena Garcia and @Tom Nguyen on 2026-02-27.
2026-03-01 - Elena Garcia: Reviewed proto; requested adding version field and a top-level 'compatibility_hint' enum so older runners can still tag messages. Marked as required in schema v1.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Li: Rust adapter (WIP) compiles in CI; basic e2e integration test passing locally (producer -> kafka -> compat consumer -> harness-runner). Container pushed to staging registry: ghcr.io/redwood/load-adapter:typed-2026-03-03

2026-03-05 - Performance: Ran initial canary with 50 small-sample runs. Observed scenario-level variance drop in two of three target workloads. Need more runs to be statistically confident. Dashboard link above updated.
2026-03-09 - Review feedback from SDK team: Ensure the schema exposes 'seed' and 'client_version' fields so we can group regressions by client changes. Added fields and updated proto (PR #324).

2026-03-12 - Marcus Li: Compatibility consumer PR opened. Compatibility mode will be behind flag 'harness.typed_scenarios.enabled'. Once compat consumer is stable, plan to flip default producer flag for nightly jobs and monitor p95/p99 deltas for 2 weeks.
notes: Trade-offs: choosing protobuf increases coupling and requires schema evolution discipline but reduces message size and improves deterministic hashing. Backwards compatibility afforded by compat consumer and feature flag should minimize disruption. We will keep legacy proxy container alive for two release cycles to give dependent teams time to migrate.
risks: Risk: Incomplete compatibility conversion could silently drop fields from legacy blobs. Mitigation: strict schema validator and round-trip conversion tests in CI
Risk: Canaries may not surface long-tail variance. Mitigation: schedule extended runs and compare goldenset + deterministic seeds
Risk: Kafka topic schema drift. Mitigation: use topic-level schema registry and require subjects for typed scenarios
